A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SEA and provide readable text, equations, figures, and tables. The complete documents were inspected: v1 ends with references and contains no appendix; v2 includes Appendices A–C. Substantial overlap supports reliable comparison despite reorganization and added experiments.

before.justification: V1 reports original SEA-PRIME benchmark results, controlled SEA ablations, language-retention measurements, and visual-token and vocabulary analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark and ablation results and adds alignment measurements, fine-grained perception evaluations, and CLIP-to-DINOv2 supervision-transfer results.

M1.justification: V2 adds cross-encoder supervision: semantic labels extracted using CLIP supervise DINOv2, extending v1's procedure based on the target vision encoder and its paired text encoder. The central similarity-weighted sampling, localized patch selection, and combined contrastive and generation objectives remain unchanged.

E1.justification: V2 adds evaluations on CapsBench, Stanford Dogs, COCO Captions, OCRBench, MMMU, and MMVP (Tables 3 and 5), substantially extending coverage of detailed captioning, fine-grained recognition, OCR, reasoning, and visual discrimination. The original eight benchmarks and named training corpora remain.

E2.justification: V2 removes the S2-Wrapper versus S2-Wrapper+SEA comparison from Table 2, although S2-Wrapper remains a comparator in Table 1. The main Table 1 comparator set is unchanged; the new perception evaluations continue comparing LLaVA with and without SEA.

E3.justification: V2 introduces TACS evaluation on 200 COCO test images with manually annotated captions, t-SNE analysis using approximately 100 COCO val2014 images with Qwen2.5-VL captions, and four-choice Stanford Dogs evaluation. It adds a 224-pixel DINOv2 configuration and removes the 1008-pixel S2 ablation. Appendix B also revises the stated vocabulary from 41,242 dictionary words to approximately four million corpus-derived and dictionary words; this does not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds embedding-distribution analysis (Figure 2), joint TACS/POPE training trajectories (Figure 5), and cross-encoder label-transfer analysis (Table 5). It removes v1's vocabulary similarity/utilization analysis and high-resolution S2 ablation. The language-retention analysis and vision-encoder unfreezing ablation remain, with the latter moving from Table 3 to Table 4.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, uncertainty bars, or significance tests. V2's additional training trajectories and evaluation-image sampling do not introduce an uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial results while preserving Table 1, retained Table 2 scores, the unfreezing ablation, and Figure 3. New baseline/SEA results include COCO CIDEr 84.8/88.7 and DINOv2 MMVP 31.3/32.0; DINOv2 MM-Vet instead changes from 20.9 to 20.8. New alignment findings accompany these results, while S2 ablation and vocabulary-analysis results disappear. The reported 7.61% Gemma gain summarizes scores already present in v1.

T1.justification: V2 introduces a formal modality-gap quantity based on nearest-word embedding distance (Equation 5) and defines TACS as an average of the ten highest visual-token matching scores (Appendix C). The original SEA mathematics is retained, and no theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The central claims remain token-level supervised alignment, preservation of language capabilities, benefits across model sizes and encoders, particularly for smaller models, and no additional training data or inference overhead. V2 foregrounds these claims and quantifies the existing Gemma benefit without changing the main contribution's substance.

C2.justification: V2 develops the explanation that misalignment consumes language-model capacity, interprets TACS/POPE correspondence as evidence for alignment quality, and extends applicability through cross-encoder transfer. Its fine-tuning discussion also proposes preservation of semantic alignment during domain adaptation. V1's specific cautions about encoder dependence, optimal token positioning, and possible loss of visual information are removed from the limitations discussion.

D1.justification: Appendix B replaces the fixed dictionary specification with corpus-based syntactic extraction and vocabulary expansion. V2 also documents caption provenance and sampling for its new alignment evaluations. Optimizer, epoch count, hardware, training times, and SEA-PRIME encoder learning rate are retained in Appendix A; their relocation is not new reproducibility information.

R1.justification: V2 adds recent MLLM and multi-encoder context, including Qwen2/2.5-VL, LLaVA-OneVision, and OmniFusion, plus references for new benchmarks. Several references supporting v1's encoder-limitations discussion disappear. The main positioning of SEA against coarse alignment approaches remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, problem discussion, and conclusion, adds an explicit contribution list, and reorganizes the experimental narrative. Related work moves from Section 2 to Section 5, training details move to appendices, and limitations become a separate section. The author list also changes.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column main layout, combines v1 Figures 1–2 into Figure 1 and Figures 4–5 into Figure 4, and adds t-SNE and alignment-trajectory figures. It removes the vocabulary figure, adds two tables, and restructures Table 2. The retained MMLU figure is reduced in size and recaptioned.

improvement.justification: V2 better supports the central alignment explanation through quantitative diagnostics and targeted perception evaluations, while DINOv2 transfer partially addresses v1's stated encoder limitation. These benefits support a net improvement. Its extent is limited by removal of vocabulary and high-resolution analyses, loss of specific limitations, and an unexplained relationship between the substantially revised vocabulary specification and unchanged retained results.
